prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: Checkout UI Strings (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "Key" · longest unbreakable unit 206px · widest one-line content 206px
  col 2: header "English" · longest unbreakable unit 62px · widest one-line content 196px
  col 3: header "中文" · longest unbreakable unit 18px · widest one-line content 184px
  col 4: header "日本語" · longest unbreakable unit 25px · widest one-line content 283px
  col 5: header "العربية" · longest unbreakable unit 55px · widest one-line content 187px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 360px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). At 360px some words cannot fit unsplit. Horizontal scrolling is ALLOWED: the table may be wider than 360px (column widths summing to more than 359px) (the reader scrolls), or you may fit within 359px and accept the consequences. Fitting and scrolling layouts are judged as two separate classes; propose good layouts of BOTH kinds.
Rendering convention: a full render shows the WHOLE table; anything right of the dashed box is not clipped — it is reached by scrolling. Where a layout scrolls, an extra "viewport view" image shows only what is visible at first sight.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Your understanding: {"purpose":"Present checkout interface strings by stable key and language so readers can find a string and inspect its translations.","tasks":["Look up a string by its key, then read the corresponding language cell.","Compare translations across a row for meaning and completeness.","Scan keys or a language column to review the set of strings."],"relations":["Each row connects one identifier with equivalent strings in four languages.","The key is the anchor for identifying a row; language headers identify the values to compare."],"roles":["The header row labels the identifier and each language.","The first column contains row headers that identify strings.","The remaining columns contain English, Chinese, Japanese and Arabic strings of equal structural importance."],"keep_whole":["Keep identifiers intact where space permits; splitting them makes lookup harder.","Keep words, numbers and short semantic units together where possible.","Keep language headers legible and associated with their columns."],"may_wrap":["English and Arabic phrases may wrap at word boundaries.","Chinese and Japanese text may wrap at natural character boundaries, avoiding awkward breaks within meaningful units where possible.","In a viewport-fitting layout, identifiers and some words must split because their unbreakable widths exceed the available column widths."],"same_scale":["The four translation columns have the same structural role, but their widths can differ to accommodate their scripts and content.","The key column deserves enough space for identifiers in scrolling designs because it anchors every lookup."],"h_vs_v":"A fitting table exposes all languages at once but forces severe wrapping and tall rows. A wider table preserves identifiers and improves reading, at the cost of horizontal scrolling and losing some columns from the initial view."}

Image 1 is the one-line content overview. Then real browser renders of: d1r1A, d1r1B (full view, then viewport view), d1r0B (full view, then viewport view).
Measured facts:
d1r1A: column widths [118, 66, 48, 65, 62] px · table 360×999 px · row heights [60, 106, 153, 292, 83, 106, 199] · column headers on >1 line: 4/5 · tallest cell 12 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 45 · fits the 360 px viewport (no scrolling)
d1r1B: column widths [227, 145, 115, 190, 145] px · table 823×325 px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 36, 36, 60] · column headers on >1 line: 0/5 · tallest cell 2 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 1 · WIDER than the viewport by 463 px (horizontal scrolling)
d1r0B: column widths [227, 150, 105, 150, 125] px · table 758×371 px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 83, 36, 60, 60] · column headers on >1 line: 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 2 · WIDER than the viewport by 398 px (horizontal scrolling)

Look at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design: what works, what is visually wrong, and the cause (which width). Then either propose up to 3 improved designs (refine the most promising, fix what you saw, or try an important unexplored idea) or, if further changes would not bring a meaningful improvement, set "done": true. Do not resubmit near-identical widths.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"best":["your best design name(s) so far"],"done":false,"designs":[{"widths":[int px],"change":"what and why"}]}
